newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodian opposition asks for ASEAN protection.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian opposition asks for ASEAN protection.

text.p: Cambodian politicians who fled their country after last month's coup said on Monday they did not trust strongman Hun Sen and wanted an ASEAN security force to ensure their safety in their homeland.
Cambodian leader Hun Sen, who ousted his co-premier and seized power in a July 5-6 coup, has urged opposition politicians to return to Cambodia and on Monday said he would guarantee their safety.
He made the comments after a meeting at the weekend with envoys from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) who were trying to find a way to solve the crisis in Cambodia.
But members of the newly-formed opposition movement, the Union of Cambodia Democrats (UCD), told a news conference in Bangkok they did not trust Hun Sen and his guarantee.

The UCD comprises the Khmer Nation Party of opposition leader Sam Rainsy, the FUNCINPEC party of ousted co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, the Khmer Neutral Party and the Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party.

"We do not trust the promise of Hun Sen to guarantee our safety so we will return when there is a mechanism set up to guarantee our safety," said Ahmed Yahya, a FUNCINPEC member of parliament who fled to Thailand last month.

Many members of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and its sympathisers left Cambodia after the prince's ouster. They included some 23 FUNCINPEC MPs and at least three MPs from the Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party, Sam Rainsy said.
He said others were in hiding in Cambodia. Human rights workers say about 40 opposition politicians were killed in a crackdown after the July 5-6 fighting in the capital.
Sam Rainsy said the opposition politicians would consider returning to Cambodia if ASEAN security forces agreed to provide security and escort them back.
"We can consider some additional or alternative guarantee," said Sam Rainsy.

"(Like) protection by some ASEAN forces. I should mention countries not neighbouring to Cambodia, like Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines -- those forces were in Cambodia already during the UNTAC (United Nations Transitional Administration of Cambodia) period so they could help...the security of some of our people," he said.
Cambodia is due to hold an election next year. The United Nations sponsored elections in Cambodia in 1993, after which Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed an uneasy coalition.
ASEAN foreign ministers said they wanted to see Cambodia sticking to its constitutional rules and hold free and fair elections as planned next year.

Hun Sen has said although Ranariddh -- who left Phnom Penh on the eve of the fighting and has not returned -- was free to return to Cambodia, he must face trial for his illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge guerrilla group.
His one condition on providing safety for other politicians was that they must cut links with the Khmer Rouge.
The UCD plans to continue its opposition campaign from outside the country until it can return.

"In the meantime our movement will actively exercise our (political) resistance against Hun Sen from outside the country and I dream that one day, maybe in the next six months we can return to Cambodia," said Ahmed Yahya.
